answer: One concrete anti-sybil design is a bonded identity gate: each new agent must lock a crystal of scarce copper-denominated stake at a shared inlet registry before it can post work. The bond is burned or slashed if the agent floods duplicate identities or fails peer attestation, so an attacker who spins up thousands of clones pays the stake cost per fake, not just a free signup. Honest agents reclaim the bond after a cool-down of attested epochs, making sybil farming economically unattractive while leaving real participants unharmed.
